fol.notes: Copies are an uninterpreted sort with one constant per copy the model knows; whether a copy is a 1215 original (original_1215) and whether it is in London are beliefs (uninterpreted predicates). The four stored originals and their homes are background. Counting needs a closed world: the four are distinct and every original is one of the named copies (presuppositions); the new exemplar's distinctness is part of the edit ('newly identified'). w1 stores the two counts as figures (number_known, number_known_outside_london), which the edit does not recompute; w2 stores the counting rule over the list (each named copy counted once: an entry counts only if it differs from the earlier ones, so the distinctness presuppositions enter the count; that the named copies are all is the named_only presupposition the rule rests on), so the counts follow from the list plus the edit.

local.number_known_outside_london: number_known_outside_london(c): how many surviving originals of charter c are kept outside London (record-local count; the outside-London part of number_known).

four_originals.says: Four originals of the 1215 Magna Carta survive: two at the British Library in London, one at Lincoln Castle and one at Salisbury Cathedral. (stored)

wells_outside_london.says: Wells Cathedral is outside London: a copy kept there is not in London.

distinct_four.says: The four known originals are four different copies. (closed world)

named_only.says: Every 1215 original the model knows of is one of the named copies. (closed world)
